assignments.reason: The sigh (אנחה) is the same essential reality as the groaning-and-sighing (נה והאנחה) already in Package 1. It is the neutral mechanism of spiritual death/severance that operates in both directions — toward holiness or toward impurity. The source text uses אנחה and נה והאנחה interchangeably throughout: 'וּכְשֶׁמִּתְאַנֵּחַ הוּא בִּבְחִינַת: תּוֹסֵף רוּחָם יִגְוָעוּן'. In eitza edge 2149, אנחה is the cause that produces rope-switching, but its essential nature — the sigh itself — is the death-process described in Package 1.

assignments.node_id: נפסק מהחבל שהיה מקשר מתחלה ונתקשר לחבל אחר כפי האנחה
assignments.reason: Being severed from the original rope and connected to another rope 'according to the sigh' describes the rope-switching mechanism itself — the structural effect of the mini-death. This is not polarized toward good or evil; the text states it works in both directions ('כְּפִי הָאֲנָחָה' — according to the nature of the sigh). Its essential nature is the same as the death-process in Package 1: the moment of severance-and-reattachment that the sigh enacts. The Rebbe frames this as the neutral mechanical consequence of the תוסף רוחם moment, which is the core bechina of Package 1.

One who sanctifies himself is explicitly equated with being connected to the holy rope: 'מִי שֶׁמְּקַדֵּשׁ עַצְמוֹ מְקַשֵּׁר עַצְמוֹ בְּחֶבֶל דִּקְדֻשָּׁה'. The essential nature of this node is holy self-consecration — it belongs to the domain of קדושה. The additions file already identifies מקדש עצמו as belonging to Gap Package B, and this CE node (edge 1943) is the same concept with the fuller phrase 'מי ש-' prefix. It is the good-pole actor in the Torah's binary of sanctification vs. defilement.

Connecting oneself to the holy rope IS the state of holiness — it shares the same essential nature as חבל דקדשה (the holy rope itself, already in Gap Package B). The text presents this as the defining action of one who sanctifies himself. Its essential nature is attachment to the domain of holiness, which is the core identity of Package B.

assignments.node_id: מי שמתאנח ונה על עברות שבידו, ורוצה לשוב בתשובה
assignments.reason: The penitent who sighs over his sins and wishes to return in teshuvah belongs by essential nature to the domain of holiness. The Rebbe describes this person as one oriented toward קדושה — the sigh is his vehicle for attaching to the holy rope. While the sigh mechanism is neutral (Package 1), the person who directs the sigh toward repentance and longing for God is essentially a holy actor. His essential identity is the yearning for holiness, placing him in the חבל דקדשה domain.

assignments.node_id: נגוע ונאסף מן הרע שהיה בידו, בבחינת: "תוסף רוחם יגועון", ונדבק אל הקדשה
assignments.reason: This outcome-node describes dying away from evil and clinging to holiness. Its essential nature is the state of being attached to קדושה — the endpoint is clearly in the holy domain. The phrase 'וְנִדְבָּק אֶל הַקְּדֻשָּׁה' (and he clings to holiness) explicitly places this node in the good polarity. While it contains the mechanism-language of 'תוסף רוחם יגועון', the node as a whole describes the positive outcome of the penitential sigh — arrival at holiness.

assignments.node_id: להתאנח על מעשיו שאינם טובים, ולכסף ולהשתוקק בתקף אנחתו לשוב להשם יתברך
assignments.reason: The Torah's practical conclusion: sighing over one's bad deeds and yearning with the force of the sigh to return to God. This is the Torah's eitza — the holy advice. Its essential nature is the orientation of the sigh toward God ('לָשׁוּב לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ'), which is unambiguously in the domain of holiness. The Rebbe presents this as the positive application of the sigh-mechanism, making it essentially a holy-rope concept.

assignments.node_id: נפסק מחבל דטמאה, ונתקשר בחבל דקדשה
assignments.reason: Being severed from the impurity rope and connected to the holy rope describes the completed transition to holiness. Unlike the neutral 'נפסק מהחבל שהיה מקשר מתחלה ונתקשר לחבל אחר כפי האנחה' (which is direction-neutral), this node specifies the direction: FROM טומאה TO קדושה. Its essential nature is arrival at the holy-rope domain. The endpoint defines the polarity — this is the good outcome, the goal of the penitent's sigh.
